newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch stocks sweep to new closing high.
newsitem.headline: Dutch stocks sweep to new closing high.

text.p: Dutch blue chips swept to a new record close on Thursday as Wall Street's opening surge gave added support to the AEX, already buoyed by gains in several major component stocks.

The AEX closed up 7.46 points at 856.59, battering through its previous record close of 849.99 set on Monday. Earlier in the session it touched an all-time high of 861.03, outpacing Tuesday's intra-day record of 855.99.
The market reversed its initial weakness early, heading into positive territory on strong demand for Dutch PTT, which continued to ride high on its demerger plans.
The stock closed up 3.40 at 82.80 guilders, back from an earlier record of 83.70.

Dealers said investor demand was being fuelled by reports of the company's break-up value. "If you keep saying that the combined worth of the postal and telecommunications activities is some 85-95 guilders per share, investors will start believing you sooner or later," one trader said.

"We're seeing the same demand as we saw for Philips earlier this week," said another. "Players have been caught out by the demand and many are being forced into buying back their shorts at higher levels."
Philips was one of the session's losers after its recent gains, shedding 3.20 guilders to 134.60 on profit taking.

Dealers said the selling pressure came mainly from Britain after a report in Thursday's Financial Times tempered enthusiasm over the Dutch electronics giant's link-up with Lucent Technologies of the U.S.
Its decline impacted on the index early, but the shares' fall was later offset by gains in other AEX heavyweights such as insurer Aegon which ended 1.50 guilders up at 138.50.
Dealers said selling pressure resulting from the share swap to acquire Providian had eased and buyers were stepping back in.

They said the Providian deal had initially led to more Aegon offering from investors in the U.S, where many pension funds are not allowed to hold stock in companies not listed on the S&P 500. Now this had tailed off, Aegon was coming back strongly, they said.
Steel maker Hoogovens surged 5.60 guilders to 108.10, after earlier touching a new all-time high of 111.00 on reports of strong U.S. demand for continental European steel.
"Given Hoogovens strong position in the United States, it is really benefiting from this news," one dealer said.
Dealers said a two-day corporate presentation to analysts earlier this week had been well-received.
Also helping the index was Royal Dutch Petroleum which more than recouped Wednesday's loss, rising 2.70 to 402.20 guilders.
Bourse newcomer Brunel International profited from the upbeat sentiment, gaining 0.50 guilders to 44.70 on its first day of listing in brisk trade.
